title: TUI theme engine: tokens to ANSI, light and dark, NO_COLOR
goal: Turn the design tokens into styled terminal output for every colour tier and theme (dark, light, high-contrast), with NO_COLOR handled by styles and glyphs instead of colour, and expose it to Ink components through a provider and hooks.
scope_in: Token resolver reading the build output of packages/theme (lane C009): all semantic tokens from DESIGN §4.2 (`bg.*`, `border.*`, `text.*`, `accent.*`, `signal`, `status.*`, `status.*.subtle`, `focus.ring`) for modes `dark` (Abyss), `light` (Shallows) and `hc` (DESIGN §19.5 values).

Tier mapping per DESIGN §19.3: truecolor hex; xterm-256 via the pinned table for the 13 listed tokens and nearest-colour search (6x6x6 cube or 24-step grey ramp, squared RGB distance) for the rest; ANSI-16 slot names; none = bold/dim/reverse only.

Option `statusColors: 'ansi' | 'hex'` (default `ansi`): status and signal tokens use ANSI names so they inherit the user's terminal theme, hex is used for brand moments (mascot, wordmark) and when set to `hex`.
`<ThemeProvider>`, `useTheme()`, `useToken(token)` returning Ink props `{color?, backgroundColor?, bold?, dimColor?, inverse?}`, and a string helper `theme.paint(token, text)`.
Glyph set with ASCII fallbacks: status glyphs `✓ ! ✗ i`, bullets `● ∴ └ ※ ▸`, box drawing; fallbacks when `unicode:false`: `v ! x i`, `* ~ \ # >`, `+-|`.

Member colour function `memberColor(slot, selfSlot)` per DESIGN §3.2 and CT-WS-SESSION-EVENTS slots: self violet, others red, yellow, green, brown in slot order skipping self, sixth participant violet with `outlined: true`; always paired with initial and name by callers.
Runtime theme switching (`setMode`) re-renders instantly with no transition; `auto` uses `queryBackground` (lane C031) and falls back to dark.
scope_out: Capability detection (lane C031) and token generation from tokens.json (lane C009).
Mascot palette handling and half-block rendering (lane C033).
build_against: Tokens JSON from packages/theme (lane C009) read from assets/theme/tokens.json in tests; terminal caps are hand-built `TermCaps` values from lane C031. No backend.
interfaces: `type ThemeMode = 'dark' | 'light' | 'hc'`; `type Token = keyof SemanticTokens` (generated from packages/theme)

`interface Theme { mode: ThemeMode; tier: ColorTier; style(token: Token): TokenStyle; paint(token: Token, text: string, extra?: {bold?: boolean; dim?: boolean; inverse?: boolean}): string; glyph(name: GlyphName): string; setMode(m: ThemeMode | 'auto'): void; subscribe(fn: () => void): () => void }`
`createTheme(deps: {caps: TermCaps; tokens: ThemeTokens; mode: ThemeMode | 'auto'; background?: 'dark'|'light'|'unknown'; statusColors?: 'ansi'|'hex'}): Theme`
`memberColor(slot: number, selfSlot: number): {name: 'violet'|'red'|'yellow'|'green'|'brown'; hex: string; outlined: boolean}`; `toXterm256(hex: string): number`
acceptance: For the 13 tokens in DESIGN §19.3 the 256-tier output equals the table indices (e.g. `signal` -> 86, `text.muted` -> 68, `bg.base` -> 233) and the 16-tier output equals the slot (e.g. `signal` -> cyan, `status.danger` -> red, `text.muted` -> blue).
`toXterm256('#7C5CFF')` returns 99 and nearest-colour search is deterministic (ties resolved to the lower index) over a 1,000-colour property test.

With tier `none` (`NO_COLOR=1`) the output of `paint` contains no `ESC[3x/4x/38/48` colour sequences; emphasis uses bold/dim/reverse only, and every status renders as glyph + word (e.g. `✗ error`, not just red).
`light` mode uses the Shallows values from the token file for all `text.*`, `bg.*` and `status.*` tokens; `hc` mode yields bg.base `#000000`, text.primary `#FFFFFF`, borders `#FFFFFF` on truecolor.
`statusColors:'ansi'` at tier truecolor emits ANSI 32/31/33/36/34 for success/danger/warning/signal/info and hex only for `accent.primary` brand uses; `'hex'` emits 38;2 sequences.
`memberColor(2,0)` = red, `memberColor(3,0)` = yellow, `memberColor(0,2)` = violet for self, `memberColor(5,0)` = `{violet, outlined:true}`; slot 1 when self is slot 1 maps to the next free colour.
`setMode('light')` triggers exactly one subscriber notification and the next frame uses new colours; no animation or interpolation exists.
Snapshot of a sample screen (header, message blocks, diff lines, permission box) renders identically per tier across 4 tiers x 3 modes, stored as 12 snapshots at 80x24.
tests: theme/tiers.test.ts: pinned table values for 256 and 16 tiers.
theme/quantise.test.ts: nearest-colour search incl. property test.
theme/no-color.test.ts: scan output for colour SGR codes; status glyph+word check.
theme/snapshots.test.ts: 12 tier/mode snapshots via lane C008 harness.
guardrails: MUST NOT hard-code hex values outside the token file and the pinned 256/16 tables; components never import hex.
MUST NOT convey meaning by colour alone; every status helper returns a glyph and a word alongside any colour (DESIGN §16.2).
MUST NOT use blink; italic and underline never carry meaning alone (DESIGN §5.4).
MUST NOT assign the red/yellow/green/brown body colours to anything except members; red never means error (DESIGN §3.2).
MUST keep the same member's colour stable for the session lifetime; colour derives only from slot and selfSlot, never from join order seen locally.
MUST treat unknown token names as `text.primary` and log once at debug.
failure_modes: tokens.json missing a token for a mode -> fall back to the dark value for that token and report via the returned `warnings`; never throw at render time.
Background query returns `unknown` in `auto` -> use dark and keep the user-visible mode label `auto (dark)`.
Unknown member slot (negative or non-integer) -> treat as slot 5 (outlined violet) and log at debug.
notes: DESIGN §19.3 says both 'truecolor: use token hex directly' and 'use ANSI names for status so the user theme is inherited'. This card resolves it with the `statusColors` option defaulting to `ansi`; confirm with design. The `hc` mode is marked 'planned' in DESIGN §19.5; values are taken from that section.
